findings.oracle: No monkeypatch: the real QMessageBox.question dialog is driven by clicking its real Yes/No button via QTimer; test_confirmed_repair_writes_real_checksum_and_fires_notify asserts the repaired CheckSum + exactly one DATA_MODIFIED event, while test_declined_dialog_leaves_checksum_unwritten_and_silent clicks No and asserts the stored checksum is unchanged and zero DATA_MODIFIED events, so removing/inverting the Yes gate goes red.

No stub: a real intellicrack_hexcore.HexDocument is opened over a real minimal 64-bit PE built by _build_minimal_pe64; oracle is document.verify_pe_checksum()['calculated'] (hexcore PE algorithm), asserted equal to the post-repair stored value and to the exact 4 little-endian bytes read back at the real checksum offset.

test_large_file_crc_stays_within_ui_memory_budget now asserts BOTH semantics and resource: crc_value == zlib.crc32(body) & 0xFFFFFFFF (independent oracle) AND UI-thread tracemalloc growth < 10 MiB on a 50 MiB file, so a streaming-but-wrong CRC fails on value and a correct-but-slurping impl fails on memory; correctness is additionally cross-checked on file/mmap/document paths and the empty-file boundary.

No spy: _RealPowerShellSandbox.run_command executes the exact production PowerShell verbatim through real powershell.exe (only the guest Create('...') path is remapped to the host shared folder) against a real owned child process; oracle is the OS-written MINIDUMP_MISC_INFO ProcessId decoded from the produced dump, asserted == requested target_pid and != os.getpid(), plus assertions that GetCurrentProcess() is absent and $targetPid/OpenProcess/CloseHandle/finally are present; the OpenProcess-failure path (System pid 4) asserts a SandboxError and no dump file.
